claims.claim: Qualys links enterprise cyber-risk reduction needs to cloud-delivered asset visibility, vulnerability and exposure-management tooling; recurring demand is supported by expanding attack surfaces, while the structural bottleneck is converting visibility into prioritized remediation within crowded security stacks.
Scenario resilience depends on platform consolidation value and integration depth being sufficient to resist substitution by endpoint, cloud-security and broader security-platform vendors.

risks.risk: Broader security suites can absorb exposure-management functions, reducing standalone differentiation if integration and remediation value do not keep pace.

unknowns.unknown: Current sources do not establish customer retention or module-level cross-sell durability.

claims.claim: Two sequential guidance raises and double-digit Q2 growth support execution credibility, but do not prove competitive share gains, retention quality or durable acceleration beyond the disclosed range.

The strongest falsifier is evidence that suite consolidation or competing platforms materially weaken retention, expansion or pricing while headline revenue still grows; no such present contradiction is established by the current evidence.

risks.risk: Growth is moderate relative to faster-growing security peers, increasing the importance of retention, cross-sell and competitive differentiation evidence.
Guidance raises are execution evidence but can still reverse; forward achievement is not assumed.

unknowns.unknown: Retention, billings quality and competitive win/loss data are not established by the current reused sources.
